findings.summary: The adapter pattern is a software design pattern that resolves interface incompatibility between two classes. It introduces a separate adapter class that translates calls from a client expecting a target interface to the existing adaptee class. This allows the adaptee to be reused without modifying its source code. The pattern is commonly applied when integrating legacy or third-party components whose interfaces do not match the client's expectations, enabling cooperation through translation rather than code changes.

mechanisms.title: Object adapter delegation
mechanisms.explanation: The adapter contains an instance of the adaptee class and delegates method calls to it at runtime, implementing the target interface in terms of the adaptee's specific operations.

mechanisms.title: Class adapter inheritance
mechanisms.explanation: The adapter inherits from the adaptee class at compile-time, thereby implementing the target interface through inheritance of the adaptee's specific operation.

unknowns: Runtime vs compile-time binding behavior in specific language implementations
Performance overhead introduced by the translation layer
Thread-safety guarantees when adapter wraps shared adaptee state
Interaction with polymorphic dispatch when multiple adapters are composed
